svg.aria-label: Table of five rejected designs and the chosen one: conditional DELETE everywhere, unique hot names with a pointer or a cold lookup, per-key busy markers, cold tombstones with a serial release, and write ids in object metadata, each with what it does and the break that rejected it. The chosen design is one journal entry per key.
svg.title: Why this shape: the designs that were tried and why each lost
svg.text: Why this shape: what was tried, and the break that ended each design
Design
What it did
Why it lost
Conditional DELETE
everywhere
Eviction, delete and release all use DELETE
If-Match on the tag just read.
MinIO ignores a conditional DELETE and RustFS does not enforce
it. And a content tag is the same before and after a delete and
a byte-identical re-put, so even an honoured condition removes
the new object.
Unique hot names, with a
pointer or a cold lookup
Each write lands under a unique hot name; a
pointer, or a cold lookup on every GET, finds
the live one.
A hot hit stops being one round trip at the client's key. A
pointer layer serves deleted or replaced keys for as long as it
is cached. Gates and stripes fail when a delayed request is
retried.
Per-key busy markers
A marker object says a key is busy; every
destructive act first lists for markers.
Every destructive act needs a LIST first, which is slow and not
atomic with the act. Its own attack review found one fatal gap.
Cold tombstones with a
serial release
A delete leaves a tombstone in cold; no cold
object is ever deleted, and tombstones expire
by lifecycle.
Uploads were aborted at a 60 s deadline, which is a size cap on
uploads that the data path does not allow. Several hot orphan
windows could still serve deleted bytes.
Write ids in object
metadata
Every write carries a unique id in its
metadata; a delete or evict names the id it
saw.
A format change to every stored object in both tiers (dir:
needs a sidecar or xattr; metadata surviving multipart
completion is unverified). And it still needs the store to act
on the id atomically, which a store that ignores conditional
DELETE cannot.
One entry per key, in hot
A small object per key being changed: create-
only, changed by If-Match compare-and-swap,
released by its holder.
Chosen. Actors take turns on one key in one atomic place; no
conditional DELETE; the hot hit stays at the client's key; the
object is also the work queue.
